narrative.overview: Specter behaves like a quiet browser instrument: live state is legible at a glance, while configuration reads as a durable local record. The popup compresses Origin to Global to Site to Tab into one signal path, and the settings page expands the same language into an indexed ledger.
keyCharacteristics: Flat paper and ink surfaces separated by hairlines.
Cobalt for actions; lime and green only for live state.
Large, compact Ubuntu headings paired with Ubuntu Mono data labels.
Rectangular controls with restrained corners and explicit ON/OFF state.
One authored trace motion, with reduced-motion fallback.

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Cobalt always means an action or focus target; lime and green always mean live protection state. Do not exchange their roles.

rules.name: The Color-Plus-Words Rule
rules.body: Every colored state must also expose an explicit label, switch text, or structural change.

rules.name: The Data-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace communicates a browser value, measurement, status code, or shortcut. It is not a decorative technology voice.

rules.name: The Paper-First Rule
rules.body: Add depth with paper tone and a rule before adding shadow. A shadow must describe an actual lifted or transient surface.

dos: Do preserve the Origin to Global to Site to Tab reading order anywhere protection state appears.
Do use literal state labels and keep controls keyboard accessible.
Do reserve bounded panels for complete instruments, forms, or task contexts.
Do verify every primary and support destination remains reachable at narrow widths.
donts: Don't replace the ledger with same-sized stacks of generic setting cards.
Don't use remote fonts, icon services, or runtime UI frameworks.
Don't use lime for ordinary actions or cobalt as the only proof of protection state.
Don't introduce pill-shaped switches, floating action controls, ornamental grids, or theatrical hacker styling.
